title: A Diagnostic Protocol for GNNs in Electricity Load Forecasting: Separating Parameter Sharing from Neighborhood Access
abstract: arXiv:2610.35074v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: A graph neural network (GNN) forecasting a collection of load series combines two mechanisms, sharing parameters across series and reading neighboring series, and a gain over a non-graph model may come from either; telling them apart decides whether a graph is worth maintaining. We propose a model diagnostic protocol that compares the GNN with three reference models: a per-node network, a network shared across nodes without neighbors, and the same GNN without edges. Degree-preserving rewiring tests whether neighbor identity matters. After a tuned benchmark on regional load in France and on low-voltage feeders in the UK, we apply the protocol to deliberately short node histories, as when non-stationary demand leaves only recent observations relevant: the feeders, within one week, and a public dataset of client consumption series. translated_title: 面向电力负荷预测的图神经网络诊断协议：区分参数共享与邻域访问
translated_abstract: 图神经网络（GNN）在预测一组负荷序列时结合了两种机制：跨序列共享参数和读取相邻序列，而相对于非图模型的性能提升可能来自其中任何一种；区分这两者决定了是否值得维护图结构。我们提出了一种模型诊断协议，将GNN与三个参考模型进行比较：逐节点独立网络、跨节点共享参数但不访问邻居的网络、以及去掉边的同一个GNN。通过保持节点度数的重新连线测试来检验邻居身份是否重要。在法国区域负荷和英国低压馈线数据上完成调优的基准测试后，我们将该协议应用于刻意缩短的节点历史场景，例如当非平稳的需求变化使得只有近期观测仍然相关时：馈线数据在一周之内，以及一个公开的客户用电序列数据集。在馈线数据上，参数共享恢复了节点特定模型与GNN之间的大部分误差差距，约
tldr: 该论文提出一种诊断协议，通过将GNN与多个参考模型（逐节点网络、无邻居的共享参数网络、去边GNN）对比来分离参数共享与邻域访问在电力负荷预测中的各自贡献，从而判断图结构是否值得维护。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes a diagnostic protocol that compares GNNs with reference models to disentangle the contributions of parameter sharing and neighborhood access in electricity load forecasting, determining whether maintaining a graph structure is worthwhile.
